goal.statement: more than 50% of tracked York County gutter queries holding a top-3 position
goal.why_unmeasured: Google Search Console is not connected, so no true rank data exists. coverage_pct below is a proxy for whether a page exists, NOT for rank.

uncovered: cost to replace gutters on a house
do i need gutters on my house
how much do seamless gutters cost
how much does a gutter guard cost per foot
how often should gutters be cleaned in pa
what size gutters do i need
why do my gutters overflow when it rains

techniques.name: York County town pages
techniques.hypothesis: 'gutter installation <town> pa' has buying intent, low competition, and almost no local contractor has a real page for it. One well-written town page a day builds a moat across the county that a competitor would have to spend months matching.
techniques.evidence: The five existing area pages are the site's only town-level coverage; York County has 70+ municipalities.

techniques.name: Cost and buying guides
techniques.hypothesis: Cost queries are the highest-intent traffic a contractor can get, and most contractors refuse to discuss price — which is why Angi and HomeAdvisor outrank them and then sell the lead back. Answering the price question honestly should win the click and the call.
techniques.evidence: Uncovered price-intent queries in the tracked universe.

techniques.name: Area-page link mesh
techniques.hypothesis: New town pages are orphans until something links to them. A nearby-areas mesh gets them crawled in days instead of weeks and passes local relevance between them.
techniques.evidence: Standard internal-linking practice; costs nothing to run.

techniques.name: LocalBusiness structured data
techniques.hypothesis: The map pack is where the money queries are actually won. Consistent name/address/phone in structured data on the site is the part of that Eric controls directly.
techniques.evidence: NAP consistency is a documented local-pack ranking factor.

techniques.name: Sitemap refresh
techniques.hypothesis: New pages are not crawled until they are in the sitemap.
techniques.evidence: Existing seo/gen_sitemap.py, re-run after each build.

techniques.name: Same-morning IndexNow push
techniques.hypothesis: Submitting only the URLs written this morning gets them into Bing and Copilot within minutes rather than waiting for the 03:05 full-sitemap run the following day.
techniques.evidence: IndexNow is supported by Bing, Yandex, Seznam and Naver.

techniques.name: Ask finished jobs for a Google review
techniques.hypothesis: Review count and recency are the strongest lever on map-pack rank for a service business. The profile sits at 13 reviews; competitors ranking above it have dozens. Every completed booking in the database is a customer who was never asked.
techniques.evidence: Google's own local-ranking guidance names review count and score.
techniques.notes: first step: confirm with Eric that customers may be emailed a review request after a completed job, then flip this to active. It emails real customers, so it stays off until a human says yes.

techniques.name: Weekly Business Profile posts
techniques.hypothesis: Business Profile posts keep the listing active and surface seasonal offers directly in the pack, where the hire-intent searches land.
techniques.evidence: GBP is live with ~300 monthly views and 4.2 stars.
techniques.notes: first step: OAuth access to the Business Profile API for enemo@nemoseamlessgutter.com — the engine cannot post without it.

techniques.name: NAP citations on local directories
techniques.hypothesis: Consistent citations across the directories Google cross-checks raise local-pack confidence, and several of them rank for the money queries themselves.
techniques.evidence: Standard local-SEO practice; NAP already verified consistent on-site.
techniques.notes: first step: most directories need a captcha or a phone verification, so this produces a submission pack for Eric rather than auto-submitting. Flip to active once the pack format is agreed.

techniques.name: Connect Search Console
techniques.hypothesis: The >50% top-3 goal is not measurable without Search Console. Until it is connected the engine reports coverage as a proxy and cannot tell whether it is actually winning.
techniques.evidence: seo/weekly_digest.py already contains a working GSC client.
techniques.notes: first step: create a Google Cloud service account, grant it read access to the nemoseamlessgutter.com Search Console property, and drop the JSON at seo/gsc-service-account.json (chmod 600).
